response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories o LEFT JOIN telescopes t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), s AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, telescope_count * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT s.observstation, s.telescope_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_above_average FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY share_above_average DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The set of observatories is every row in the observatories table, so stations with zero telescopes are included with a count of 0 and are part of the 'average share across all observatories'.
Share is telescope_count divided by the total number of rows in telescopes, computed as a real number with no rounding.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-observatory shares.

alternatives.interpretation: Only observatories that actually have at least one telescope are counted, so the average share is taken over those stations only (derived from the telescopes table).
